yield-curve-inversion.title: How long did the U.S. yield curve stay inverted?
yield-curve-inversion.question: How many days was the 10-year minus 2-year U.S. Treasury yield spread negative in 2022–2025?
yield-curve-inversion.description: Four yearly Treasury files with different columns each year, merged into one daily 10-year minus 2-year spread.
yield-curve-inversion.source: U.S. Treasury · Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates
yield-curve-inversion.finding: The 10-year minus 2-year spread was negative on 541 of 998 business days, from 1 April 2022 to 5 September 2024, and reached −108 bp on 3 July 2023.
yield-curve-inversion.verification: Every daily spread, the inverted-day count and the streak match an independent plain-Python reference; the yields are checked against the Treasury files and the spread against the yields.
yield-curve-inversion.caveat: Par yields, not zero-coupon rates. An inversion describes the curve's shape on those days; it is not a forecast.
yield-curve-inversion.operations: Merging files with different columns · date parsing · spreads · run lengths
review_notes: Chart: spread line, zero line, inverted area filled only below zero — correct.
Explanation matches the results and states the par-yield and no-forecast limits.

jump-option-prices.title: How do price jumps change option values?
jump-option-prices.question: How do Merton jump-diffusion option prices differ from Black-Scholes prices with the same total variance?
jump-option-prices.description: Merton jump-diffusion against Black-Scholes with the same total variance, across 13 strikes, with a fixed 21-term series and put-call parity checked in both models.
metrics: Strike with the largest put premium
jump-option-prices.finding: With the same total variance, the jump model prices at-the-money options 0.343 lower and far out-of-the-money puts higher, peaking at strike 80: jumps move probability into the tails.
jump-option-prices.verification: All 13 strikes match an independent reference to 1e-8; λ = 0 reproduces Black-Scholes and put-call parity holds in both models.
jump-option-prices.caveat: Assumed parameters; a pricing example, not a market quote.
jump-option-prices.operations: Closed forms · a fixed 21-term Poisson series · parity checks
review_notes: Chart: Merton minus Black-Scholes differences against strike; call and put differences coincide, as put-call parity requires.
Explanation: lists the difference at every strike correctly (higher below about 92, lower above) and notes the parity; its account of why (fatter tails) is brief.

eurusd-sma-costs.title: Does a trend-following strategy still pay after costs?
eurusd-sma-costs.question: Does a 50/200-day moving-average crossover on EUR/USD beat buy-and-hold after 2 bp trading costs, 2015–2025?
eurusd-sma-costs.description: A 50/200-day moving-average rule traded one day after each signal, with costs on every position change, against buy-and-hold.
eurusd-sma-costs.source: ECB · euro reference rate against the U.S. dollar
eurusd-sma-costs.finding: After costs the strategy ended at 0.933 against 1.030 for buy-and-hold, with a smaller maximum drawdown (16.5% against 23.4%).
eurusd-sma-costs.verification: Every day's equity, every trade and its cost match an independent reference; the trade list matches the position changes, and a hand-computed 8-day example checks the one-day lag.
eurusd-sma-costs.caveat: Computed by Lamuir from ECB reference rates, which are daily fixings, not traded prices. A historical test, not a forecast.
eurusd-sma-costs.operations: Moving averages · lagged execution · cost accounting · drawdowns
eurusd-sma-costs.boundary: Long or flat only; one parameter pair.
review_notes: Chart: both equity curves and the strategy drawdown in a lower panel — correct.

Explanation: the numbers match the results. Three wordings are inaccurate. It says trades execute at 'the next day's open'; the task uses the next day's ECB reference rate. It calls the 21 trades 'round-trip trades'; they are single position changes. Its claim about whipsaws was not tested.

eurusd-ewma-volatility.title: How do two volatility estimates compare?
eurusd-ewma-volatility.question: How do EWMA (λ = 0.94) and 60-day rolling volatility estimates of EUR/USD compare over 2015–2025?
eurusd-ewma-volatility.description: RiskMetrics EWMA (λ = 0.94) against a 60-day rolling standard deviation of EUR/USD log returns.
eurusd-ewma-volatility.source: ECB · euro reference rate against the U.S. dollar
eurusd-ewma-volatility.finding: In this sample the EWMA estimate peaked at 18.5% on 11 November 2022 and the 60-day rolling estimate at 14.4% on 29 November 2022. Both react on the day of a large move; EWMA weights recent days more, so its peak is higher and comes earlier here.
eurusd-ewma-volatility.verification: Both daily series match an independent reference to 1e-10; a hand-computed 3-day example and a constant-price check test both formulas.
eurusd-ewma-volatility.caveat: Computed by Lamuir from ECB reference rates. Neither estimate is the true volatility; the result depends on λ and the window length.
eurusd-ewma-volatility.operations: Log returns · rolling variance · recursive EWMA
eurusd-ewma-volatility.boundary: One currency pair; one λ and window.
review_notes: Chart: both series over 2015-2025, labelled — correct.
Explanation says EWMA reacts more quickly; consistent with this sample (the EWMA peak came first and was higher), stated as a general property rather than proved.

usd-cross-rates.title: Which currency rose most against the dollar in 2025?
usd-cross-rates.question: What was the 2025 percent change of the euro, pound, yen and Swiss franc against the U.S. dollar?
usd-cross-rates.description: ECB rates quoted per euro, turned into U.S. dollar values and a pound-yen cross, with triangle consistency checked every day.
usd-cross-rates.source: ECB · euro foreign exchange reference rates
usd-cross-rates.finding: Against the dollar in 2025 the Swiss franc gained 14.5%, the euro 13.8%, the pound 8.4% and the yen 0.2%.
usd-cross-rates.verification: Every daily rate matches an independent reference to 1e-12, and the triangle identity holds on every date.
usd-cross-rates.caveat: Computed by Lamuir from ECB reference rates, which are fixed once a day; they are not trading prices.
usd-cross-rates.operations: Reshaping long data · quote conversion · cross rates
review_notes: Chart: cumulative change of four currencies — correct.
Explanation matches the results and states that ECB rates are daily fixings.

bond-rate-sensitivity.title: How much does a bond lose when rates rise?
bond-rate-sensitivity.question: How much would a 10-year, 4%-coupon bond's price fall if its yield rose 100 bp from the end-2024 10-year Treasury yield?
bond-rate-sensitivity.description: A hypothetical 10-year, 4% annual-coupon bond priced at the end-2024 Treasury 10-year yield: duration, convexity and a one-point rate rise.
bond-rate-sensitivity.source: U.S. Treasury · Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates (10-year, 31 December 2024)
bond-rate-sensitivity.finding: At a 4.58% yield the bond is worth 95.43. A one-point rise cuts the price to 88.14, a 7.64% fall; duration alone predicts a slightly bigger fall, and convexity closes most of the gap (error 0.014).
bond-rate-sensitivity.verification: Every cash flow, the price, duration, convexity, the shocked price and all 25 points of the price curve match an independent reference; a par bond priced at its own coupon rate checks the pricing.
bond-rate-sensitivity.caveat: Hypothetical bond; the Treasury par yield is used as its yield to maturity. Not a quote for a real Treasury bond.
bond-rate-sensitivity.operations: Reading the latest yield · discounting · duration and convexity · repricing
bond-rate-sensitivity.boundary: One fixed-coupon bond; parallel yield shift.
review_notes: Chart: exact price curve with the duration-only and duration-plus-convexity approximations over ±300 bp — correct.
Explanation: the numbers match the results; it explains duration, convexity and why the duration-only line lies below the exact curve, and states that the bond is hypothetical.
